Brătianu holds an important place. Photo: memorialulsighet.ro Steliu Lambru , 13.09.2026, 14:00 Among the leading figures in 20 th -century Romanian historiography, Gheorghe I. Brătianu holds an important place. Gathered around the ‘Revista Istorică Română’ (Romanian Historical Magazine) in the 1920s, the young scholars of that time, Constantin C. Giurescu, Petre P. Panaitescu, Gheorghe I. Brătianu, and others, proposed new principles of historical methodology to move away from the positivist thinking that had prevailed until then and founded the New School. In that spirit, Brătianu excelled through his writings and was considered by many to be the leader of his generation. Born on January 28, 1898, in Ruginoasa, Iași County, Gheorghe I. Brătianu was the son of the Liberal politician Ion I. C. Brătianu and his first wife, Princess Maria Moruzi-Cuza. Although he held a law degree, Brătianu was deeply drawn to history, which he studied at the Sorbonne. There, in 1929, he earned his doctorate with a dissertation on Genoese trade in the Black Sea region during the 13 th century. As a product of the French educational system, Gheorghe Brătianu was influenced by the French Annales School of historiography. He was a university professor and a member of the Romanian Academy. Among his extensive historical works, the volumes ‘An Enigma and a Historical Miracle: The Romanian People’, ‘The Historical Tradition Concerning the Founding of the Romanian States’, and ‘The Black Sea’ are the best known and most highly regarded. Like other young people of his generation, Brătianu fought on the front lines of World War I and was involved in politics. Furthermore, Brătianu also took part in the fighting in Crimea during World War II until 1942. He was married to Princess Elena Sturdza, with whom he had three children, and died in detention at the Sighet prison at the age of 55. He is considered one of the symbols of Romanian patriotism. When he was offered the chance to leave for France to avoid arrest, he reportedly said, ‘A Brătianu never leaves his country.’ As a politician, Brătianu led a faction of the National Liberal Party that was close to the authoritarian regime of King Carol II. Although a Francophile, during World War II Brătianu advocated for an alliance with Nazi Germany. After the communist regime took power in 1945, Brătianu was arrested and imprisoned in Sighetul Marmației, like most Romanian democratic politicians. In a 1996 interview with the Oral History Center of Romanian Radio Broadcasting Corporation, another prominent Romanian historian, Petre Ș. Năsturel, recalled the circumstances leading up to the arrest of Gheorghe I. Brătianu in 1950: “I knew Professor Brătianu, but I hadn’t majored in history, I’d majored in Greek, Latin, and Byzantine philology. But the professor cared about me and even wanted to hire me at Iorga’s Institute of History, which he headed. But one day, a grim day, Professor Gheorghe Brătianu, along with other internationally renowned researchers and scholars, was forced to stay at home. The question arose of how to get the publications to them so they could continue working from home and how to get their papers published. And so an entire network was organized, involving Mrs. Elena Brătianu, the professor’s wife, Professor Mihai Berza, myself, and a French Catholic priest, Father Emil Jean, who had remained at what had been the French Institute of Byzantine Studies on Christian Tell Street.’ It was the excellent relations between Romania and France that saved Brătianu’s work. In those days, when the terror of Stalinism reigned, everything seemed hopeless. Petre Ș. Năsturel gave further details: “This French priest, through the French Embassy, sent Brătianu’s unpublished works, books and articles, to Paris to a great friend and scholar, Father Vitalien Laurent. And so, everything that escaped destruction is due to this chain of goodwill and Romanian dignity, with France’s help. Later, the works appeared in Paris, Munich, and elsewhere, but they were preserved as part of Romania’s cultural heritage. And after a number of years, Brătianu’s works, printed in France and Germany, were translated into Romanian so that they would be accessible to our fellow Romanians back home.” Today, when we look back, everything seems easier, simpler, and some even allow themselves the luxury of nostalgia. But back then, everything was a matter of life and death. Petre Ș. Năsturel is back at the microphone with details: “It was very dangerous, most dangerous of all for Brătianu, who ultimately met his end in the torments of Sighet Prison. It was also very dangerous for Mihai Berza, who at the time had two young children. It was also dangerous for me, who at the time had neither a wife nor children, but I had my parents living with me, whom I supported financially. But we all did our duty, and that is something that must be known. In the West, I realized that people imagine that Romanians remained passive under the insidious Soviet-Romanian communist occupation. There were people among us who knew how to fight; some fell, some died in prison, and others escaped. I am among those who escaped.” Gheorghe Brătianu was one of Romania’s great historians of the 20 th century. Long blacklisted for political reasons, he was restored to the Romanian public consciousness in the name of freedom after 1989. (LS) Share pe Facebook Share pe Whatsapp Tags: Gheorghe I. https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-commi.text: The European Commission has told capitals to reduce demand for gas and electricity in a bid to tame prices amid a global energy crunch. "In the context of constrained global supply and high price volatility, demand reduction can be an effective tool to contain prices," EU Commissioner for Energy and Housing Dan Jørgensen wrote in a letter to EU ministers, dated Sept. 25 and seen by POLITICO. In the letter, Jørgensen invites ministers to take measures to reduce demand for gas and electricity "for as long as necessary." He argues that while the situation is "challenging", there are "currently no immediate risks to security of supply." Advertisement Advertisement Gas storage levels in Europe are currently at historic lows as the war in Iran disrupts global gas flows, which could set up the continent for an expensive winter. Storage levels currently sit at 68% of capacity, which is well below the 71% measured at the same period in 2021 — just before the start of a historic energy crisis in the wake of Covid-19 and the start of the war in Ukraine. The EU has a baseline target to have gas storage filled to 90% by the start of November, but some flexibility was granted on this in March , allowing countries to aim for 80% this year to avoid panic buying and alleviate costs. Measures taken by EU countries to regulate prices should be "well-targeted" and "temporary", Jørgensen's letter reads, to avoid a surge in demand.

https://evertiq.com/news/2026-10-01-icey.text: © Nokia ICEYE Electronics Production | October 01, 2026 ICEYE and Nokia to build sovereign satellite communications for governments Evertiq Finnish satellite company ICEYE and Nokia are partnering to develop broadband satellite communications systems in low Earth orbit (LEO) that governments can own and operate themselves. The first communications satellites are expected to launch in 2028. The systems are aimed at defence, border security, emergency services and disaster response, according to a press release from ICEYE and Nokia. Customers will own and control the satellites, the ground segment and the terminals. The aim is to give governments communications that stay available when terrestrial networks are disrupted or compromised. The systems will provide high-throughput, low-latency connectivity over priority mission areas. They are designed to complement existing military and commercial networks, not replace them. "Nations must be able to fully own and control their communications, without dependency on a foreign commercial operator's terms of service," says Rafal Modrzewski, CEO and co-founder of ICEYE. Under the partnership, ICEYE brings its experience delivering sovereign satellite missions, and Nokia contributes secure networking technology from its growing defence portfolio. Together, the companies will integrate satellites, ground infrastructure and ruggedised terminals. For ICEYE, the deal extends the business model it already uses for radar satellites, where nations buy their own systems, into communications. According to Modrzewski, the company delivered Poland its own radar satellite system in under a year. The companies have not disclosed any customers, the size of the investment or the number of satellites planned. Beállítom Melania Trump közvetítésével helyi tűzszünet jöhet létre Oroszország és Ukrajna között a háború sújtotta Oleski városában, ami lehetővé tenné a humanitárius segélyek célba juttatását és a civilek evakuálását – jelentette be pénteken a Fehér Ház. Az amerikai kormány szerint a helyi tűzszünet október 29-én lépne életbe – írta az AP hírügynökség . A Fehér Ház közlése szerint az egyeztetéseket az amerikai first lady kezdeményezte. Melania Trump egy megbízottja közreműködésével közvetlenül az orosz és az ukrán vezetés képviselőivel tárgyalt a tűzszünet feltételeiről. Az ukrán kormány egyelőre nem kommentálta a bejelentést. Az TASZSZ közlése szerint Valerij Geraszimov orosz vezérkari főnök pénteken bejelentette, hogy október 27-én, moszkvai idő szerint hajnali 4 órától az orosz hadsereg tűzszünetet vezet be a Herszon megye orosz ellenőrzés alá vont részén lévő Oleski közelében, az ott végrehajtandó humanitárius művelet miatt. Donald Trump amerikai elnök felesége kiemelt ügyének tekinti a háború sújtotta gyerekek megsegítését: az év elején az ENSZ Biztonsági Tanácsában is ülést szervezett ebben a témában. Ezen kívül személyes levelet írt Vlagyimir Putyin orosz elnöknek, hogy elősegítse az orosz–ukrán háború miatt elszakított gyerekek és családtagjaik újraegyesítését. A Dnyeper folyó partján fekvő Oleskiben hónapok óta súlyos élelmiszer- és gyógyszerhiány alakult ki. A folyó választja el az ukrán erőket a várost megszállás alatt tartó orosz csapatoktól. A Herszon megyei városban nincs áram, fűtés és vezetékes víz. A városból kivezető utakat elaknásították, az út mentén kiégett autók sorakoznak, a drónok blokád alatt tartják a települést. A korábban 24 ezer lakosú várost az orosz csapatok a 2022-ben indított teljes körű invázió első napján foglalták el. Az épületeket ágyúzások rongálták meg, sok közülük leégett, a létfontosságú infrastruktúra pedig súlyos károkat szenvedett. Újabb katasztrófát okozott 2023 júniusában a Nova Kahovka-i gát felrobbanása , amelynek nyomán a víz elöntötte a várost . Az AP tényfeltáró vizsgálata arra jutott, hogy a robbanást nagy valószínűséggel az orosz hadsereg okozta. A katasztrófában több száz ember vesztette életét. A városban maradt civileket most az éhínség és a betegségek fenyegetik, miközben újabb kemény tél közeledik. Ukrajna többször is helyi tűzszünetet sürgetett annak érdekében, hogy megszervezhessék a civilek kimenekítését. Oroszország azonban mindeddig nem vállalt erre kötelezettséget, noha megszálló hatalomként a nemzetközi jog értelmében köteles lenne gondoskodni arról, hogy az ellenőrzése alatt álló területeken élő civilek hozzájussanak a túlélésükhöz szükséges alapvető ellátáshoz.
